# Asset and licence manifest

## Summary

**All visual assets are generated by code at run time.** No third-party
models, textures, audio files, fonts or images are bundled in the repository
or production build. Quran audio streams from MP3Quran.net. The recorded
Haram adhan streams from a version-pinned public mirror described below.
No recordings are bundled with the project.

After `npm install` fetches the code dependencies, `npm run build` and the
visual simulation work offline. Quran and adhan playback require internet access to
the external providers. The scene remains a procedural reconstruction, with
no photographic reference textures.

Only `three` is present in the shipped bundle. Everything else is a build- or
development-time tool.

## Generated assets

Each of these is produced by a named function at start-up. The "cost" column
is measured, not estimated; see TEST-REPORT.md.

| Asset | Generator | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Marble (3 tones) | `env/Materials.ts` → `marbleTexture` | Value-noise veining over a flat base, at 128–512 px depending on quality |
| Kiswah cloth | `env/Materials.ts` → `kiswahMaps` | Twill weave height field → colour, normal and roughness maps |
| Dressed stone (2 tones) | `env/Materials.ts` → `stoneMaps` | Coursed ashlar with offset joints, plus a derived normal map |
| Gold relief | `env/Materials.ts` → `goldReliefMaps` | Abstract interlace only — see "What is deliberately absent" |
| Sky dome | `env/Environment.ts` → `buildSky` | Gradient shader; also the source for the pre-filtered environment map |
| Contact shadow | `characters/CrowdRenderer.ts` | 8-segment disc with a radial alpha ramp |
| Character mesh (3 LODs) | `characters/CharacterMesh.ts` | Ring-based procedural body, garment, head, limbs |
| Character animation | `characters/AnimationBank.ts` | 19 clips, baked to a vertex-animation texture at start-up |

## Streamed Quran recordings

| Item | Source / behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Reciter | **عبد الرحمن السديس — Abdul Rahman Al-Sudais** |
| Recitation | Hafs from Asim, murattal; all 114 surahs |
| Provider | [MP3Quran.net reciter page](https://www.mp3quran.net/ar/sds) |
| Metadata | [Public API, reciter 54](https://www.mp3quran.net/api/v3/reciters?language=eng&reciter=54), listed as “Abdulrahman Alsudaes” in English |
| Stream URLs | `https://server11.mp3quran.net/sds/001.mp3` through `114.mp3` |
| Implementation | `audio/AudioSystem.ts`, using the browser audio player |
| Usage permission | [MP3Quran.net copyright statement](https://www.mp3quran.net/eng/privacy), verified 2026-09-07, permits visitors and developers to copy material and use links |

The provider documents its audio metadata in its [public API
documentation](https://www.mp3quran.net/eng/api). The recordings are referenced
by URL and are not bundled with the application.

The app attempts audible autoplay when it is ready. If the browser blocks
autoplay, it retries on the user's first click, tap, or key press. The main-screen
**speaker icon** or `M` pauses and resumes at the same position. A deliberate pause disables
automatic retries, so later interactions do not restart playback.

Playback starts at Al-Fatihah, advances through all 114 surahs in Quran order,
and stops after An-Nas; a new play request after completion starts at
Al-Fatihah again. Playback preserves the recording's original speed and is
independent of the simulation clock and prayer events. A connection or
playback failure displays an error with a retry action.

## Streamed Haram adhan

- Recording: regular **أذان الحرم المكي 1 — علي بن أحمد ملا**, Sheikh Ali Ahmed Mulla.
- Original attribution: [Islamweb recording page](https://audio.islamweb.net/audio/index.php?audioid=1&page=audioinfo).
- Playback mirror: [Kiwifu/adhan-mp3](https://github.com/Kiwifu/adhan-mp3), file
  `Ali_Ibn_Ahmad_Mala_1_-_Al_Haram_Al_Maki_(علي_بن_أحمد_ملا_-_الحرم_المكي).mp3`,
  pinned to commit `b9180a2bb769f74cff8e378ef2cc7aaf8db5cd5b`.
- Source configuration and playback: `src/audio/AdhanPlayer.ts`.
- Verified duration: 246.412 seconds. The original and mirrored file report
  492,824 bytes. Attribution follows the source and mirror labels; this is a
  referenced third-party recording, not a project-owned or generated asset.

The original audio host requires its own page referrer; the HTTPS mirror is used
for cross-site playback. **Call to prayer** or `P` plays the recording once,
pausing Quran first. Completion or prayer cancellation restores Quran only if
it was enabled beforehand. The speaker icon stops adhan without resuming Quran.
Simulation reset cancels adhan and restores the prior Quran choice; leaving the
page stops both. Recorded audio is independent of the simulation clock.

## What is deliberately absent

**No Qur'anic calligraphy.** The kiswah of the Kaaba carries Qur'anic text
woven in gold thread, and the hizam — the belt around it — is one of the most
recognisable pieces of Islamic textile art in the world. This simulation does
not attempt to reproduce any of it. The hizam and the door are rendered as
gold bands and panels carrying abstract geometric relief. Generating
approximate, wrong, or invented Arabic script on a sacred object would be
disrespectful and inaccurate at the same time, and no amount of texture
resolution would fix that.

The same restraint applies to the arcades and the minarets, which in the real
building carry inscription friezes.

**No crowd noise, iqamah or takbir audio.** The former generated noise has been
removed. The manual call uses the recorded adhan described above. Iqamah and
takbir events are signalled visually and in the event log.

**No photographic reference textures.** See above.

**No real individuals.** The crowd is procedurally generated. Height, build,
gait phase and garment colour vary per agent from a seeded random source. No
agent is modelled on, or intended to resemble, any specific person.

## Reference sources used for dimensions

These informed the numbers in `src/config/site.ts`. They are sources for
*measurements*, not assets — nothing was copied into the project.

- Widely published Kaaba dimensions: 13.1 m high, sides of 12.86 m and
  11.03 m; shadharwan approximately 25 cm high with a 35 cm projection; door
  sill approximately 2.13 m above the courtyard.
- The corners of the Kaaba point approximately to the cardinal directions,
  with the Black Stone at the eastern corner.
- Hijr Ismail: a low semicircular wall off the north-western face, commonly
  given as about 1.32 m high and 0.9 m thick.
- Maqam Ibrahim: approximately 11–13 m from the Kaaba, in front of the door.
- The mataf was a 95 m diameter circle before the expansion; the post-2016
  ground-level open area is substantially larger, with roughly ten
  entrances and exits.
- Masjid al-Haram has 13 minarets; Saudi-era minarets around the central
  precinct are commonly given as about 89 m, and the King Abdullah expansion
  minarets as about 139 m.
- Pedestrian data: free-flow preferred walking speeds around 1.0 m/s with a
  standard deviation of about 0.2 m/s, with slower cohorts; observed mean
  speed close to the Kaaba wall under Hajj density falls to roughly 0.33 m/s,
  with local densities reported up to 7–9 persons per square metre.

Published figures disagree with each other in several of these cases,
particularly for the Hijr and for the post-expansion mataf. Where they did,
the value chosen is noted in `src/config/site.ts`. The model is a dimensional
reconstruction assembled from published figures, **not** an architectural
survey, and it should not be used as one.
